title: Egg and Bacon Sandwich on Croissant

content.title: About
content.content: The egg and bacon sandwich on a croissant combines a buttery flaky croissant, crispy bacon, and a creamy egg filling. It is usually served warm, sometimes with cheese, herbs, or a sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The croissant originated in Austria but became a French icon.
Bacon is traditionally made from pork belly, though turkey and plant‑based versions exist.
Eggs in the sandwich are often poached or scrambled to keep a soft texture.
Egg‑and‑bacon sandwiches are a staple of breakfast menus worldwide, from American diners to European brunch spots.
The contrast of buttery pastry, salty bacon, and rich egg creates a highly satisfying flavor profile.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and bacon provide complete protein needed for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Both ingredients supply B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Bacon contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Butter‑based croissant offers monounsaturated fats that can be part of a balanced diet in moderation.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Egg yolk is one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: High saturated fat and sodium
items.content: Bacon and buttery pastry can raise cholesterol and blood pressure if eaten frequently.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: The combination of croissant, bacon, and egg makes the sandwich energy‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may contain salmonella; ensure eggs are fully cooked.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People with egg allergy should avoid this product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, sliced in half. It pairs well with lettuce, tomato, avocado, or a drizzle of hollandaise. For a lighter version, choose a whole‑grain croissant and lean turkey bacon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, refrigerate wrapped tightly for up to 24 hours. Croissants can be frozen for up to 2 months, and bacon for up to 1 month when sealed in airtight bags.
